correctionFromCP1.what: CP1's design (a single unbounded (county_fips, rail_key)-scoped SQL statement, measured 408.8ms on the smallest county 48055) does not survive contact with the largest program counties. Live-measured: the same unpaged shape -- tried in three forms (a parcel_record JOIN, a place_key LIKE-prefix filter, and a place_key range filter, all against the actually-idle store per pg_stat_activity) -- timed out at 120s+ on county 48453 (Travis, 380,917 parcels). EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, no ANALYZE) on the JOIN form showed the planner choosing a Seq Scan on parcel_record (Travis is ~39% of that table, past the county_fips index's selectivity threshold) feeding a Nested Loop of 380K individual index probes; the range form showed an Index Scan on parcel_record_cell_pkey with an estimated Total Cost of 1,380,343 (5x the join form's 265,108) -- both plans are expensive for the same underlying reason: parcel_record_cell's PK orders rows by (place_key, rail_key), so a WIDE place_key range with an equality filter on the TRAILING rail_key column cannot skip the ~64 other rails per parcel without walking them (no skip-scan for this index shape).
correctionFromCP1.fix: loadCountyRailCells now pages internally via loadCountyRailCellsPage (LIMIT 500 by default, ordered by place_key, cursor = last row's place_key) and accumulates in JS memory across pages before calling evaluateRailGate once on the full accumulated set. Each page statement only ever touches page_size x 65 leaf entries regardless of county size. This is the actual 'streaming/batched per rail' the mission's own wording names -- CP1's initial reading (one statement, scoped to one rail, as opposed to the whole-county 65-rail loader) was an incomplete interpretation; the real dead-end was any UNBOUNDED per-county statement, not merely an unscoped-by-rail one.
correctionFromCP1.liveValidation: County 48453 (Travis), rail 'flood': 762 pages, 380,917 cells accumulated correctly (matches parcel_record's own count -- the integrity check passed), 139.9s wall time end-to-end via the CLI, 100-180ms per individual page statement. This is the SAME county and rail that timed out unpaged at 120s+. A Cloud Run job (task-timeout=21600s per the existing cloudbuild.parcel-record-fill.yaml pattern) easily absorbs 140s for the single largest program county; the scheduled job in this card's Factory half will run once per (county, live rail), not once total, so per-call cost is bounded and this is not a scaling cliff for the scheduler.
